conventions: React + Tailwind. Theme tokens via CSS variables on :root / [data-theme]. Prefer a small context + hook over a state library. Persist preference in localStorage. Keep it additive; do not restyle existing components beyond swapping hardcoded colors for tokens they already use.

gates.build: npm run build && npm run lint
gates.testSetup: Jest + RTL for any unit bits. For visual/interaction verification use the Chrome DevTools MCP against the dev server (`npm run dev`, default http://localhost:5173). Frontend behavior is verified by driving the browser, not by unit tests.

plan:
## Feature
Add a light/dark mode toggle. A theme provider sets `data-theme` on <html>, persists the choice to localStorage, and defaults to the OS `prefers-color-scheme`. A toggle button in the header switches it. Frontend/visual feature — verified by driving the browser, not unit tests.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A toggle in the header switches between light and dark; the change is visible immediately (background + text colors flip via tokens).
- The choice persists across a page reload.
- On first visit with no stored choice, the theme follows the OS `prefers-color-scheme`.
- No regression: existing pages render correctly in light mode exactly as before.

## Integration Points
- ThemeProvider wraps the app in src/main.tsx (or App root).
- Toggle button rendered in src/components/Header.tsx.
- Dark token overrides added to src/styles/theme.css under [data-theme="dark"].

## Implementation Steps
1. Add src/theme/ThemeProvider.tsx: context + useTheme hook; read localStorage then prefers-color-scheme; set data-theme on document.documentElement; expose toggle.
2. Add dark-mode CSS variable overrides in src/styles/theme.css.
3. Add a ThemeToggle button to Header.tsx.
4. Wrap the app root with ThemeProvider in main.tsx.

## Files
- src/theme/ThemeProvider.tsx
- src/components/ThemeToggle.tsx
- src/components/Header.tsx
- src/styles/theme.css
- src/main.tsx

## Test Strategy
kind: manual
unit: false
method: chrome-devtools-mcp
details: Start the dev server (`npm run dev`). Using the Chrome DevTools MCP, load the app, click the header toggle and confirm the background/text colors flip; reload and confirm the choice persists; clear localStorage and confirm it follows the emulated prefers-color-scheme. Build + lint must pass. If the DevTools MCP is unavailable in the run environment, report not-run so the orchestrating agent verifies interactively.

## Gate
green
